facts.fact: The Ghana National Household Registry page describes a single national database that serves as the primary platform for identifying and targeting beneficiaries of LEAP, school feeding and national health insurance (NHIS) enrolment; no date is given for the statement, so the page's published year is used.

facts.fact: MoGCSP's terms of reference say its social protection programmes and other systems operate in silos with data dispersed across systems, limited interoperability and each programme running its own servers, and seek a firm to build a unified data exchange platform linking them to the National ID Registry.

facts.fact: At a Technical Working Group meeting on 29 January 2026, NDPC said fragmented data management limits sharing across Ghana's social protection systems, and the project consultants said the several platforms remain poorly linked with limited access across institutions, particularly at sub-national level.

MoGCSP reported progress toward full integration of its social protection management information systems to centralise data and enable real-time monitoring, reviewed at a World Bank GPSNP 2 support mission; the article is undated and its date is inferred from the mission of 20-24 October 2025.

facts.fact: The policy says the registry links its data with the NIA, NHIA, GES and other MDA databases, and shares aggregated or de-identified data with authorised MDAs for interoperability.
The policy says registry data identifies beneficiaries for several programmes, namely LEAP, NHIS and school feeding.
The policy says the registry holds the NIA Ghana Card number and links its data with NIA (ID), NHIA (health) and GES (education).
